findings.title: M6 late vendors must also re-render the crafting-list vendor badges
findings.body: The plan (batch 1, M6) makes vendors.json a separate promise that lands after the core nine files, but only names the quests tab as its consumer. The crafting list uses the same data: app.js:445 injects `vendorHtml: (iid) => CraftQuests.vendorHtml(iid)` into CraftList, and crafting-list.js:214 calls it for each shopping material. CraftList only calls render() inside init (crafting-list.js:285) or when the list changes (add, addRuns, removeOne, delete, qty), and it has no public refresh. Today loadData awaits vendors before CraftList.init, so a saved list shows 🏪 price badges on first paint. After M6, if vendors arrive after init, those badges stay missing and nothing signals it until the user edits the list. Files and acceptance cover only app-render/app-quests/app-data/app-browse/app.js and quest-tab checks. The plan should add crafting-list.js to Files with a list re-render when vendors arrive late (or keep vendors in the core set). It should also add an acceptance check: 5-second-late vendors, then the saved crafting list shows its vendor badges.

findings.title: Seed staging with existing inputs for partial and in-place modes
findings.body: Batch 2 points every module's OUT at a fresh staging directory, and the partial flags "only update their own files". Two partial modes, however, read existing files out of OUT. `--consumables-only` rewrites meals.json and medicine.json in place: consumables.py:16-18 records a problem and skips when the file is missing. `--quests-only` reads OUT/recipes.json in write_job_quests (quests.py:165), and write_vendors reads OUT/recipes.json and ingredients.json (quests.py:259-261). Those files are only created in the full path, by copy_static_data. With an empty staging dir, both entry points will always fail with PROBLEMS and exit 1, breaking the plan's own "四種入口維持範圍" acceptance. Also, since each module does `from .common import OUT` at import time, reassigning common.OUT is not enough; every read site must follow the redirect. The plan should state the precondition: before running a partial mode, copy that mode's inputs (meals/medicine, or recipes/ingredients) from data/ into staging, and publish only that mode's output files. Staging should also sit on the same volume as data/ so per-file os.replace can publish; build-data.py itself notes that drive letters differ per machine.

findings.title: Assign S-items fixed this round to a batch with acceptance checks
findings.body: The plan says S1, S2, S3, S4, S6, S7, S9 and S12 are "直接清理, 本輪confirmed", yet none of them is placed in a batch, given an order, or given acceptance checks. Some change behavior. S7 changes readiness display in app-flow.js, a file outside batch 1's list. S9 changes how build-notices.py resolves CARGO_HOME, which affects the output of the notices build. S2 deletes assertions from tools/tests/30-solve.test.mjs while batch 1 (M4/M6) may also need to change the frontend tests, so the same file has overlapping edits. S1 deletes app.js proxies while batch 1 also restructures app.js loadData. Without a batch and acceptance checks, the final unified run cannot tell whether a change to S7's UI or S9's notices output is intended or a regression. The plan should either fold these into batch 1 (app.js, app-flow.js, tests) and batch 3 (build-notices) with matching acceptance checks, or mark them explicitly out of scope for this round.
